_doc: The single-source-of-truth registry: each CAPABILITY has exactly ONE home; all callers use it. Read by the honestreview `single_source_of_truth` doctrine (write-time) and tests/test_canonical_concerns.py (suite). Adding a concern is a deliberate act: give it a home, a one-line description, and a `telltale` (what its operations look like, so a reviewer can locate candidate sites). `status`: 'enforced' = one home today, the gate checks it; 'consolidating' = home chosen, callers still being moved. See docs/SINGLE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md.

concerns.description: A model's maximum OUTPUT tokens (published cache > live catalog > learned-fact-floored > backstop); NEVER below OUTPUT_FLOOR unless a genuinely-published max is lower. The ceiling is not the cost.
concerns.telltale: resolving or clamping a per-model output-token ceiling / max_output for a call or estimate

concerns.description: The OUTPUT max_tokens actually SENT for a call: the ceiling (output_ceiling) as the cap, the 32K floor as the minimum, scaled to the classified output type; the CALLER'S requested max_tokens is IGNORED (spendguard owns it). Every send path calls this — none decides the budget itself.
concerns.telltale: deciding the max_tokens value to send on a model call (floor/ceiling/caller-value/recommend math)

concerns.description: Whether the INPUT fits the model's input window — REFUSES an over-window input, never truncates it. Input is never silently clipped anywhere.
concerns.telltale: checking or bounding input/prompt size against a model input window; any slice of prompt/content fed to a model

concerns.description: Mapping a requested reasoning tier (minimal|low|medium|high) to the reasoning_effort value a given model actually accepts (only the floor varies per model).
concerns.telltale: translating a reasoning tier to a wire reasoning_effort per model

concerns.description: $/token and realtime/batch cost from token counts; the single price table and cost math.
concerns.telltale: computing dollars from token counts, or reading per-token rates

concerns.description: The canonical predicate for 'this exception IS a deliberate spend/budget refusal or deadline that must propagate, never be swallowed by a fail-open handler.'
concerns.telltale: deciding whether an exception is a deliberate stop / refusal to re-raise

concerns.description: The ONE $0 snapshot of the admission + queue + reasoning-economics picture that the CLI (`spendguard dispatch`) and the MCP tool render identically.
